evidence: 2025 trip report: 'mostly class 2 scrambling with a couple of class 3 moves' to the summit; 2018 party: class 2 scrambling on the north side of the summit block.

fix.rock_grade: Class 3 (brief exposed moves at the summit block)

note: No source reports anything harder than Class 3; the record's 'Class 3-4' summit moves are unsupported.

evidence: 1972 AAJ first-ascent report: 'three leads of class five on granite, the last being a very sharp crest', then 'three leads of class three and four' to the summit; no number given anywhere.
note: Searched peak name, route, FA party names (Williamson/Bucher/Oas), with 5.x terms; the AAJ account is the only route-specific source and gives no YDS number. 5.0 per the low-5th rule; may be harder.

evidence: 2020 report via the NW gully to the ridge: loose class 3 then 'a short section of exposed class 4 just below the true summit'; hike2hike: final ridge 'several class 4 moves', '3rd and 4th class'; SummitPost: summit block '4th class/low 5th' for ~20 ft.
note: Two reports from this line call the crux class 4; only SummitPost mentions low 5th as one variation of the 20-ft summit block, so Class 4 rather than 5.0. Snow/verglas on the ridge can make it harder.

evidence: Castle Creek/south-face ascent: '3rd class blocky terrain' between 7,600 and 8,000 ft; a WTA report on the NE gully/7,400-ft notch line calls it class 3+ and says class 4 can be unavoidable once snow has melted; onehikeaweek confirms the line (south gully, NE gully at 6,800 ft toward the notch) without a class.
note: Late season, when the snow is gone, a short Class 4 step may be unavoidable per one report.

evidence: No graded write-up of the Chair-Bryant line found; the overlapping Tooth-Chair Traverse on MP is 5.4 (Grade III), '4th/low 5th sub par rock', one short mandatory rappel off Bryant.
note: Searched route name variants, FA names (Ari Schneider, Jason Linker), Chair north ridge, MP Chair and Bryant area pages: nothing grades this traverse. Chair's NW ridge is a class 3-4 scramble. Nothing supports the record's 5.7.

evidence: Green Creek Circuit report: the west ridge is 'a weird return to actual hiking before some final fun scrambling to the true summit'; no class given.
note: Searched Cinderella Peak with class terms, SummitPost, CascadeClimbers (East Buttress TR is a different, harder route: 4th class with bits up to mid-5th), AAJ Twin Sister High Route, Mountaineers traverse page (403). No source grades the west-ridge finish; record's Class 4 kept but it may be Class 3.

evidence: 2016 report on this line (NW couloir, north ridge, west-face headwall): headwall 'Class 5.8+ or 5.2/A1', loose Class 4-5 ledges, Class 4-5 ridge to summit. Another climber's summary: final summit climb is 'a 50 foot fun rock corner (5.5)' with 3 fixed pitons. 1963 AAJ: gully/chimney system 'class 5'.
note: Sources disagree on the summit pitch: 5.8+ (estimated by a party that aided it) vs a 5.5 corner with fixed pins (possibly a different summit-tower line). Kept 5.8+ as the only figure tied to this exact line; could be 5.5.

evidence: AAJ 2005: first winter ascent (Miller/Taylor) found 'difficult mixed climbing low in the couloir and straightforward snow-climbing' above; no summer YDS grade found anywhere online; record's 5.6 kept.
note: Searched NE/North Face Couloir, Kloke Simon, Kloke Couloir, winter-ascent names, SummitPost (blocked), AAJ. FA year conflicts: Wikipedia says 1972, Burdo's AAJ note says 1974, record says 1976. Burdo's 1988 IV 5.10 chimney may be the melted-out version of this line.

evidence: Alpine Institute: 'warm up on 40-50 deg. snow and ice for about 800 ft of the First Couloir'; Mountaineers: ~45 deg for ~800 ft; Climber Kyle: 'steep and exposed snow, with some possible ice to the right', climbed unroped.
note: Steep snow (40-50 deg) mapped to Class 3; no source gives an ice grade for this couloir alone (the AI3/WI3 of Triple Couloirs is the runnels above it). Icy conditions could justify AI2. The alpine_grade III fits the full Triple Couloirs, not this couloir alone.

evidence: Trip report: steep snow gully to the East-West col, 'some 4th class' to the saddle, then 'easy 3rd class terrain to East McMillan's summit'; a 2025 North Buttress party 'downclimbed SW to the col with West McMillan' before rappelling.

fix.rock_grade: Class 4 (4th class to the col, 3rd class to the summit)

note: The 5.6 belongs to West McMillan's side of the col, not East McMillan; MP's 'no non-technical route' is consistent with a Class 4 step plus glacier/steep snow.
